title: Optimization of an acid digestion procedure for the determination of Hg, As, Sb, Pb and Cd in fish muscle tissue
author: Mohammed, Mohammed, et al.
materials: Materials•Polyethylene bags, (Ziploc, USA)•Ice•Stainless steel food processor (Hamilton Beach)•65% Nitric acid, 37% Hydrochloric acid and 30% Hydrogen peroxide- ACS grade, (Sigma-Aldrich, USA)•Whatman 541 filter paper, (Sigma-Aldrich, USA)•Heating block (VWR reaction + heating block)- capable of exceeding 150 °C, (VWR, USA)•Acid washed volumetric flasks (50 mL-Class A) and (25 mL-Class A), (Pyrex, USA)•50 mL Pyrex boiling tubes, (Pyrex, USA)

Instrumentation and Materials•SpectrAA 880 Varian Atomic Absorption Spectrophotometer (Varian Inc. USA)•Agilent vapor generation accessory VGA-77 (Agilent technologies Inc. USA)•AccuStandard stock solutions of mercury (1000 μg/mL), arsenic (1000 μg/mL), lead (1000 μg/mL) and cadmium (1000 μg/mL) (Accustandard, USA)•Inorganic Ventures stock solutions of selenium (1000 μg/mL) and antimony (1000 μg/mL) (Inorganic Ventures, USA).•Tin (II) chloride, reagent grade, 98%, (Sigma-Aldrich, USA)•Sodium borohydride, ACS grade, (Sigma-Aldrich, USA)•Sodium hydroxide, ACS grade, (Sigma-Aldrich USA)•Hydrochloric acid, ACS grade, (Sigma-Aldrich, USA)•Potassium iodide, ACS grade, (Sigma-Aldrich, USA)•Hot plate, VWR reaction + heating block, (VWR, USA)

steps.title: Gather materials and equipment
steps.instruction: Collect all required items: polyethylene Ziploc bags, ice, stainless‑steel food processor, 65 % HNO₃, 37 % HCl, 30 % H₂O₂ (ACS, Sigma‑Aldrich), Whatman No. 541 filter paper, VWR heating block capable of >150 °C, acid‑washed 50 mL and 25 mL Class A volumetric flasks (Pyrex), 50 mL Pyrex boiling tubes, SpectrAA 880 Varian AAS, Agilent VGA‑77 vapor‑generation accessory, 1000 µg mL⁻¹ stock solutions of Hg, As, Pb, Cd (AccuStandard) and Se, Sb (Inorganic Ventures), SnCl₂ (98 %, Sigma‑Aldrich), NaBH₄ (ACS, Sigma‑Aldrich), NaOH (ACS), HCl (ACS), KI (ACS), hot plate, and de‑ionised water.

steps.title: Prepare shark tissue aliquots
steps.instruction: Thaw 0.9 kg of shark muscle (collected on ice, stored at –20 °C) at room temperature, remove skin and bone, homogenise with the food processor, then weigh 0.5 g (±0.1 mg) portions into clean, dry 50 mL Pyrex boiling tubes.

steps.title: Add digestion acids
steps.instruction: To each tube add 10 mL of one of the following acid mixtures (use separate tubes for each mixture): (i) concentrated HNO₃ only, (ii) concentrated HNO₃ : HCl (3 : 1 v/v), (iii) concentrated HNO₃ : H₂O (1 : 1 v/v). All acids are ACS‑grade (Sigma‑Aldrich).

steps.title: Predigest and perform open acid digestion
steps.instruction: Leave the tubes at room temperature (≈26 °C) for 24 h (predigestion). Then place the tubes on the heating block and heat at the chosen temperature (60 °C, 90 °C, 120 °C or 150 °C) for the selected digestion time (30, 60, 90, 120 or 150 min) as listed in Table 1 for each metal/acid combination. Use a separate set of tubes for each temperature‑time condition.

steps.title: Cool, filter and dilute digests
steps.instruction: Allow the heated tubes to cool to room temperature, then filter each digest through Whatman No. 541 filter paper. Rinse the original tube and the filter with de‑ionised water, collect the filtrate and bring the volume to 50 mL with de‑ionised water in a 50 mL Class A volumetric flask. Store the diluted extracts at 4 °C until further processing.

steps.title: Prepare arsenic and antimony hydride solutions
steps.instruction: For each digest intended for As or Sb analysis, pipette 5 mL of the filtered digest into a clean boiling tube, add 10 mL of 1 % (w/v) KI prepared in 1 M HCl, heat the mixture for 4 min at 70 °C, cool, filter again through Whatman No. 541, and make up the filtrate to 25 mL with de‑ionised water.

steps.title: Prepare mercury and selenium (and other) analysis solutions
steps.instruction: For Hg, Se and any other metals, transfer 5 mL of the filtered digest into a boiling tube, add 5 mL of 1 M HCl, and dilute to a final volume of 25 mL with de‑ionised water. Process acid‑blank digests and spiked samples in the same way.

steps.title: Prepare reducing reagents and perform AAS analysis
steps.instruction: Each day prepare fresh reducing solutions: (i) stannous chloride 25 % (w/v) in 15 % (v/v) HCl for Hg and Se, (ii) sodium borohydride 0.6 % (w/v) in 0.5 % (v/v) NaOH for As, Sb and Se. Load the appropriate reagents into the Varian SpectrAA 880 AAS equipped with the Agilent VGA‑77 vapor‑generation accessory. Analyse samples in the following order to avoid cross‑contamination: first Hg and Se, then As and Sb. Use the instrumental conditions listed in Table 2 (flame‑AAS for Pb and Cd, CV‑AAS for As and Sb, HG‑AAS for Hg). Run each sample in triplicate, record results in µg L⁻¹, convert to µg g⁻¹ (wet weight), and report mean ± standard deviation.

substeps.instruction: Prepare SnCl₂ solution: 25 % w/v SnCl₂ in 15 % v/v HCl.
Prepare NaBH₄ solution: 0.6 % w/v NaBH₄ in 0.5 % v/v NaOH.
Set flame‑AAS for Pb and Cd (air/acetylene flame).
Set CV‑AAS for As and Sb (air/acetylene flame, KI/HCl pre‑reduction).
Set HG‑AAS for Hg (air/acetylene flame, SnCl₂/HCl reduction).
Analyze each diluted sample three times, calculate mean ± SD.
